refined_question: Let A, R, and S be Noetherian commutative rings over a common base, with R local having maximal ideal m_R, and let M and N be finitely generated R-modules. Decide whether each of the following statements holds in full generality: 1. (Zero Divisor Theorem) If M≠0 has finite projective dimension over R and r∈R acts injectively on M, then r is not a zero divisor in R. 2. (Bass’s Question) If M≠0 admits a finite injective resolution, then R is Cohen–Macaulay. 3. (Intersection Theorem) If M⊗_R N≠0 has finite length, then dim N≤proj dim_R M. 4. (New Intersection Theorem) For any finite complex of free R-modules 0→G_n→…→G_0→0 whose homology ⊕H_i(G_•) has finite nonzero length, one has dim R≤n. 5. (Improved New Intersection Conjecture) If in such a complex H_i(G_•) has finite length for i>0 and H_0(G_•) admits a generator annihilated by a power of m_R, then dim R≤n. 6. (Direct Summand Conjecture) For every module-finite extension R⊆S with R regular, R is an R-module direct summand of S. 7. (Canonical Element Conjecture) For any system of parameters x_1,…,x_d of R, any lifting of the identity map K_•(x_1,…,x_d)→F_• from the Koszul complex to any free resolution F_• of the residue field R/m_R has nonzero last component. 8. (Existence of Balanced Big Cohen–Macaulay Modules) There exists an R-module W (not necessarily finitely generated) with m_R W≠W on which every system of parameters is an R-regular sequence. 9. (Cohen–Macaulayness of Direct Summands) If R is a direct summand of a regular ring S, then R is Cohen–Macaulay. 10. (Vanishing Conjecture for Maps of Tor) For A⊆R→S with A, S regular and R module-finite over A, the map Tor_i^A(W,R)→Tor_i^A(W,S) vanishes for all i≥1 and every A-module W. 11. (Strong Direct Summand Conjecture) For any module-finite map of complete local domains R⊆S and any height-one prime Q of S lying over a principal ideal xR with R and R/xR both regular, the inclusion xR⊆Q splits as R-modules. 12. (Existence of Weakly Functorial Big Cohen–Macaulay Algebras) Any local homomorphism of complete local domains R→S admits functorially compatible balanced big Cohen–Macaulay R- and S-algebras B_R→B_S. 13. (Serre’s Conjecture on Multiplicities) If R is regular of dimension d and M⊗_R N has finite length, then the Euler characteristic χ(M,N)=∑(-1)^i length Tor_i^R(M,N) is zero when dim M+dim N<d and positive when dim M+dim N=d. 14. (Small Cohen–Macaulay Modules Conjecture) If R is complete, there exists a nonzero finitely generated R-module on which every system of parameters is a regular sequence. Determine which of these conjectures hold for all such rings and modules.
justification: The name ‘Homological conjectures in commutative algebra’ refers collectively to a definitive list of fourteen interrelated conjectures relating homological invariants (projective dimension, injective resolution, Tor, etc.) of Noetherian commutative rings to their intrinsic structure (Krull dimension, Cohen–Macaulay property, regularity) ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra)). However, the title alone omits crucial context: it does not specify the class of rings (Noetherian, commutative, local in certain statements), the modules involved (finite versus infinite, properties like systems of parameters and Koszul complexes), nor the precise definitions of terms such as balanced big Cohen–Macaulay algebra, module-finite extension, or the exact formulations of each conjecture in the list ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homological_conjectures_in_commutative_algebra)).
